<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via data.create (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/data/:object), data.find (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`  _(via data.create (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via data.find (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via data.create (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via data.find (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/data-service.mdx`  _(via data.create (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/data/:object), data.find (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/data/:object))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via data.find (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/data/:object))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via data.create (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/data/:object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/data/:object (route, 38 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `54ee6c2f6e123d131b66f401946b60a188a16a2f` — the merge of head `b88c632b10cf415af60c1258ccc755562cf97a73` into base `6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 54ee6c2f6e123d131b66f401946b60a188a16a2f && git checkout 54ee6c2f6e123d131b66f401946b60a188a16a2f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa b88c632b10cf415af60c1258ccc755562cf97a73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa && git merge --no-ff b88c632b10cf415af60c1258ccc755562cf97a73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T22:01Z

Head-sha: 81b6323e8684ef25a4e10d07756a8f0c30b9090c
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34897. The contract is claim amendment 6960622194 (seat-ruled route A and its three conditions) and reading 6960505974. The report is os-dev 6962163959.

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34897`, base `main`. Seven paths, +339/-43, all in `packages/qa/scenarios/**` plus one changeset:
- `orchestrate.ts`, with the new `loadSeedRows`, `seedApp`, and step 2 of `restoreSeededRows`;
- the doors doc in `app.ts`;
- `README.md`;
- the test double `test/runner/seed-door.ts`, the export fixture's `installManaged`, and five new tests.

This stays inside the claim's file surface: nothing touches `skills/**`, the cards, `packages/spec` or `packages/objectql`. `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match a runner change with no exported signature moved. Not governed.

**CI.** It was still running when I read it (16 pending, 14 success, nothing failed). This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**(1) The door.** `loadSeedRows` builds one data-only manifest, `data[]` with one dataset per object (`mode: 'insert'`, `externalId: 'id'`), and sends it through the harness's existing `installManaged`, which is `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` with `installMode: 'managed'` as the admin. That door hands `data[]` to the platform's seed loader, which writes under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`. So it is the route the reading named: only `state_machine` is skipped, and every other rule and hook still judges each row. Some details I checked:
- **One namespace per load** (`scenarioseeda`, `…b`, …, letters only). The doc measures that a second package claiming a held namespace is refused with `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`. The counter is process-wide, which is safe because each half boots its own environment.
- **Only an inline load is a load.** A door refusal, a missing managed door, or `seeded.mode` other than `inline` refuses every row with the reason in its message. So a harness that cannot seed shows up in the record and is never silently empty.
- **Ownership is unchanged for rows no persona owns.** The loader writes as system with no user, and the install-local door's `stampSeedOwner` (`marketplace-install-local-seed-owner.ts`) then sets `owner_id` and `created_by` to the caller, the admin, and only where they are empty. So "those rows keep the inserter (the admin)" in `seedApp`'s doc still holds, and a persona owner the body sets is kept (M3).

**Condition 1, ids kept as lookup targets: met.** The report's M1, measured before any code: 757 inserted, ids kept, and lookups resolve to the card ids. The re-run record agrees: `seed: { inserted: 757, refused: [] }`, with `secondPass` setting `demotravel_department.manager` ×4. The cycle pass still works after the load.

**(2) Refusals with no code: a scorecard shape change I accept.** `seed.refused[]` entries were already `{object, id, code?, message?}`, with `code` optional. Nothing in `packages/qa/scenarios/src` reads a seed refusal's `code` (I grepped every `refused` reader). `seedDrift` compares two loads that now both lack a code, so its comparison is still like for like. The loader's sentence carries the reason, and it names the record. The README says "the seed door names no error code", so a reader of an old record and a new one knows why the field is gone.

**(3) Persona ids in the load, PATCH only for cycle lookups.** The seat has ruled this A since the report, on the condition that the README and the PR body state it and why. I read the code as built. `seedRowBody` is unchanged, so `owner_id`, the persona `user` field and the handle rewrites ride in the body. The second pass still sets only `plan.deferred`. The README and body push gets a docs delta read.

**(4) Condition 2, the trigger note: met.** The README's Seed paragraph and the changeset both say seed rows fire no record-triggered flow. They name the four cards that ask for such flows and say each seeds the flow's values itself (a ticket's group, SLA policy and breach flag, a line's over-standard flag, the statuses). They also say an operation's own write still goes through the agent's door.

**(5) Condition 3, the re-run: met.** In `/mnt/project-files/issue-34897/rerun-replay/`, the ask mode on the kept `template.json` (dist `b7ab31a715d4e83c`) exited 0, with Seed `757/757`. So 0 of the 114 root refusals remain, and the 470 cascaded rows are in. The Run scores in that record come from recorded turns of the old round, so they say nothing about this change, and the PR doesn't claim they do.

**Tests and ablation.** The double (`seed-door.ts`) writes each row through the harness's own `insertRow`, so a row the double's rules refuse is refused at the door too. `TravelRulesApp` carries the kept build's rules:
- the user door refuses a paid claim;
- the seed loads all 757;
- a control trip breaking `end_after_start` takes its claim, 2 lines and 2 steps with it;
- a restore re-inserts a removed paid claim;
- a missing managed door refuses all 757 with a reason.

The ablation legs are each red on the half they revert: 4 of 5 for the seed loop, and the restore test alone for the restore.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. The reference-entry branch of `loadSeedRows` is untested.** The loader reports two kinds of `errorList` entry:
  - `field: '(write)'` for a row it could not write;
  - `field: <lookup field>` for a reference it dropped from a row it did write. That is `pushError` in `seed-loader.ts` around line 2252, and the row still lands (`referencesDropped`, framework#3932).

  The code handles both. A dropped reference counts the row as refused with `fields`, takes it out of `inserted`, and keeps its second-pass patch. A row with both kinds of entry is one refusal without `fields`. But the double only ever emits `(write)`, so none of that runs in a test. On a real host it is not hypothetical. A child whose lookup names a row the load refused, with that lookup optional in the build, lands with the link dropped instead of being refused. It is then present in the database while the tally calls it refused. Please add one test where the door's answer carries a reference entry for a written row, and pin all of these:
  - (a) the refusal has `fields: ['<field>']`;
  - (b) `inserted` is one lower;
  - (c) the row's deferred patch still runs;
  - (d) a row with both a reference entry and a `(write)` entry counts once, without `fields`;
  - (e) in `restoreSeededRows`, such a row counts as reinserted.

### Notes
- N1. Each load installs a package: the seed, every restore round that re-inserts, and each fresh copy. So an ask run can leave several `com.scenario.seed.*` packages installed. They declare no app, object or navigation, only `data[]`, so I expect the agent sees nothing new. Nothing measures what the MCP tools list after the seed, though. If a later round shows a "Scenario seed" entry in an agent's reading, this is where it came from.
- N2. The re-run's one restore came through a fresh copy (`restored: {freshCopy: [...]}`), so the live path of `restoreSeededRows` step 2 through the door has only the double's test so far. The first ask round after landing will exercise it.
- N3. The report's out-of-scope note: `order_to_cash` build 1 refused 66 payment rows on "may not exceed the invoice's open balance", and the seed loader's order and roll-up timing now decide that check. It is worth a look on the first round after landing, because a roll-up-dependent rule is exactly what the seed posture still runs.

Next: the README and body push for the seat's ruling A, and the S1 test, then an L1-c delta read. Then o3-G lands once the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed: the seat already ruled route A, and the deviation is ruled too.

## L1: ACCEPT (delta) · 2026-11-17T22:24Z

Head-sha: 1c5dbc3a450e7df76156973b377fe84529b11671
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c. This is a delta read of `81b6323e`..`1c5dbc3a` against my 6962248251.

### 席位核对

**Delta.** Two commits on top of my ACCEPTed head, three paths, +71/-4. No `src/` file moved.
- `6a38c579` (README): the Seed paragraph now says the second pass sets only the deferred cycle lookups, and why. `data[]` carries a persona's user id as sent, and patching it again would put a user-door update, with its triggers and hooks, back on every seed row. That is the condition the seat set when it ruled the PATCH point A. The PR body states it too.
- `1c5dbc3a` (S1): the double `seedDoorAnswer` takes an optional `drops`. For each dropped reference it removes the field, writes the row without it, and adds an `errorList` entry with `field` set to that lookup and the loader's "Deferred reference unresolved" sentence. That matches the real loader's `pushError` shape (`seed-loader.ts` around line 2252). Doubles that pass no `drops` behave as before.

**S1: closed.** The new test covers each point I asked for:
- (a) `dep_ops`, written without its `parent`, is refused with `fields: ['parent']` and the loader's sentence;
- (b) `inserted` is 755: 757, less `dep_fin` refused on write, less `dep_ops` counted refused;
- (c) its deferred patch still runs: `dep_ops.manager` is `e09` after the second pass, and `secondPass` counts 3 managers, because `dep_fin` is not there to patch;
- (d) `dep_fin` has both a reference entry and a `(write)` entry, and it counts once, without `fields`;
- (e) after `dep_ops` is removed, `restoreSeededRows` reports it in `reinserted`, with its manager set back.

The S1 ablation (`unheld.set` neutered) turns only this test red (756 vs 755), so the test reaches the branch it is meant to reach.

**CI.** The report says the first head's red on `Lint · docs & code guards` / `Lint & Repo Gates` was a 25-minute checkout timeout. On this head nothing has failed so far: 11 success, 18 skipped, 15 pending. This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1 to N3 of my first read stand as notes (the seed packages that build up, restore step 2 having no live run yet, and `order_to_cash` on the first round after landing). None is owed.

Next: o3-G lands once the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
